STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of cut melon (pale green flesh, likely honeydew or a similar melon) on a white square plate, photographed from directly above. There is a small orange smear (possibly juice or a trace of another fruit) near the left edge of the pile.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish white dish about 22 cm across its width. Area ≈ 22 x 22 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 400 cm². Using a round approximation, 3.14 x (11)² ≈ 380 cm²; I use ~390 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Cubed/cut melon pieces (about 12-14 pieces), each roughly 2.5-3 cm cubes; a trace of orange juice or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: Melon pieces cover roughly 22% of the plate (about 85 cm²). Orange smear is negligible (<1%). Total food coverage ≈ 22%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pieces are piled slightly, typical height ~1.5 cm. 85 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 128 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut fruit bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 128 ml x 0.6 ≈ 77 g. Round to about 80 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Honeydew/melon ~35 kcal per 100 g. 80 g x 0.35 ≈ 28 kcal. Orange juice trace: ~1 g, negligible (~0.5 kcal).

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About a dozen small cubes of melon is a plausible small side portion, roughly 70-90 g and under 40 kcal. The estimate is consistent with what is visible.

Total: about 80 g, about 28 kcal.
